title: Review: Graphs and data analysis; SI units and prefixes; Estimation and orders of magnitude; Experimental methods and practical skills
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS01-1#N.12, MS03-1#N.7, MS04-1#N.10, MS06-1#N.13, MS01-1#N.7, MS04-1#N.3, MS06-1#N.12, MS01-1#N.5, MS04-1#N.6. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Gradient
items.clue: Δy divided by Δx, taken from a large triangle; it has its own units.

items.label: Reaction time
items.clue: Delay between a signal and a person's response: about 0.2 s for an adult.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Letter such as k, M or n placed before a symbol to stand for a power of ten.

items.label: Base units
items.clue: Building blocks such as kg, m, s, A, K and mol, from which all others are made.

questions.stem: Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.stem: Two samples of ideal gas, X and Y, are sealed in rigid containers. Y's container has twice the volume of X's. Graphs of pressure against absolute temperature for the two samples are straight lines through the origin, and X's line is twice as steep as Y's. How do the amounts of gas compare?

options.text: X holds twice as much gas, because its line is twice as steep.
Y holds twice as much gas, because its container is twice as large.
They hold equal amounts of gas.
X holds four times as much gas: its line is steeper and its container smaller.

questions.explanation: Slope = nR/V, so n = slope × V/R. X: 2s × V; Y: s × 2V. The products are equal, so n is the same.

questions.stem: A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: A student has a ruler with 1 mm divisions and wants the thickness of one sheet of paper, about 0.1 mm. Which choice and reason are both correct?

options.text: Measure one sheet ten times and average, because averaging reduces the uncertainty.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because the reading uncertainty is shared out.
Measure a stack of 10 sheets ten times and average, because more readings always help.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because any calibration error in the ruler then cancels.

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?
Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: A student investigates how the time t for a ball to fall from rest depends on the drop height h. (h = ½gt², with g constant.) Which plan is best?

options.text: Drop the ball once from each of three heights, timing by hand; plot t against h.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t².
Drop a ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically, with a heavier ball for the greater heights.

questions.explanation: Enough values, repeats, no reaction time, and h = (g/2)t² gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2.

questions.stem: A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).
